script: Team owners who got fined! Ben Simmons was one of the most talked-about players in the NBA, and it had nothing to do with basketball. He was a three-time All-Star who had just demanded the Philadelphia Sixers trade him, and he made it clear he never wanted to wear their jersey again. Every team wanted to know where he'd end up, and the Golden State Warriors kept popping up as the favorite. But one man was about to open his mouth and turn a simple interview into a league investigation. His name is Joe Lacob, and when a San Francisco Chronicle reporter asked if Golden State would go get Simmons, he never actually said Simmons' name. He called him a Defensive Player of the Year candidate while he was in Philadelphia, and everyone knew who he meant. Instead of hyping him up, Lacob said the trade didn't make sense, explaining that Simmons made way too much money at thirty-three million dollars a year, and questioning whether he could even finish games. Then he compared him to his own star Draymond Green, and said the two were too similar to work together. But the reason that answer got him in trouble has nothing to do with what he actually said. One day later, the NBA fined Joe Lacob fifty thousand dollars. And here's where it gets strange. He didn't get punished for chasing Simmons, he got punished for turning him down. The league has a rule where you're not allowed to publicly talk about a player under contract with another team, whether you want him or not. So Lacob talked his way out of a trade he never wanted, and it still cost him fifty grand.
